image_description: A close-up, macro shot of the soleplate of a steam iron. The image focuses heavily on the pattern of steam holes, which appear as raised brass or gold-colored rings rather than simple perforations in flat metal. To the left, a portion of the white plastic housing is visible with standard small perforations. At the bottom, a white ceramic-like support stand (rest) is partially visible.

This is a significant structural deviation from real-world irons, where holes are flush or slightly countersunk, not protruding cylinders.
